name: Primary Interstitial Lung Disease in Childhood and Adulthood Due to Alveolar Structure Disorder
aliases: Alveolar Structural Disorder-associated Interstitial Lung Disease
Pediatric and Adult Primary Interstitial Lung Disease with Alveolar Abnormalities

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed Diagnostic Criteria for Primary Interstitial Lung Disease due to Alveolar Structure Disorder

criteria.description: Chronic respiratory symptoms including progressive dyspnea and nonproductive cough
High-resolution CT showing diffuse interstitial lung abnormalities with alveolar architectural distortion
Lung biopsy demonstrating alveolar structural abnormalities with interstitial fibrosis and inflammation
Exclusion of secondary causes of interstitial lung disease such as environmental exposures, infections, or connective tissue disease
Restrictive ventilatory defect with reduced diffusing capacity for carbon monoxide (DLCO)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all major criteria including clinical presentation, characteristic imaging, histopathology, and exclusion of secondary causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis often requires multidisciplinary evaluation including pulmonology, radiology, and pathology.

searchTerms: worsening shortness of breath with activity
fine crackles heard at lung bases
weakness related to low blood oxygen

common.symptomName: Hypoxemia at rest or with exertion
searchTerms: low oxygen levels at rest or exercise

occasional.symptomName: Weight loss due to chronic illness

rare.symptomName: Pulmonary hypertension symptoms (e.g., syncope, chest pain)
searchTerms: symptoms of high lung blood pressure
fainting and chest pain from lung hypertension
shortness of breath with chest discomfort

laboratory: Mild hypoxemia on arterial blood gas analysis
Normal or mildly elevated inflammatory markers (ESR, CRP)
Absence of autoantibodies typical for connective tissue diseases
imaging: High-resolution CT showing ground-glass opacities, reticular changes, and alveolar architectural distortion
genetic: Mutations affecting alveolar epithelial cell function and surfactant protein genes reported in some familial cases
other: Restrictive pattern on pulmonary function tests with reduced DLCO
Histopathology showing alveolar septal thickening, fibrosis, and abnormal alveolar architecture

distinguishingFeatures: Characteristic usual interstitial pneumonia (UIP) pattern on imaging and histology
History of environmental exposures, drug toxicity, or connective tissue disease
Presence of systemic symptoms or autoantibodies
Variable imaging patterns depending on cause
